provider.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1700-1701 and matched by the standard factory at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:433-435. default_model is only part of the truth: with an empty model the gateway picks a _Multimedia id from the session language (gateway/src/core/stt/ibm_watson/config.rs:600-618) and falls back to en-US_Multimedia; four of those language defaults (es-LA, zh-CN, ar-MS and hi-IN _Multimedia) are not IBM models. Every IBM model (18 large speech ids, 21 telephony ids including the beta medical one, 12 multimedia ids) is served on the WebSocket interface and on synchronous HTTP, so no IBM model needs a segmented path; file upload is a fallback, and a gateway-driven stop on the open socket is the better way to give the gateway the turn boundary. Rows are an allow-list: today any string is sent to IBM unchanged. Streaming client, as read: Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). The keep-alive is 64 bytes of silence after 10 seconds without audio (client.rs:246-263), which does not meet IBM's rule of 15 seconds of audio in any 30 second window. IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1245-1267); the evidence records no live call to IBM. Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). This model family needs audio sampled at 16 kHz or higher. The design frame records that the speech-to-text leg receives audio at the rate the caller sent it (not re-read for this row), so an 8 kHz telephone leg is below the model's minimum on this transport. IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. IBM's socket accepts many recognition requests on one connection: binary audio, then {"action":"stop"}, then the final results, then {"state":"listening"}, after which the next request needs no new start message. The gateway would keep streaming audio as it arrives and send stop when its own detector reports end of speech, so IBM finalises at once instead of waiting out its 0.8 second pause. Interim results keep arriving while the caller speaks, there is no upload, and the session uses one of the instance's concurrency slots. The latency gain is inferred from the documentation and has not been measured. It is a change to the existing client, not to the shared file-upload adapter.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST {instance URL}/v1/recognize with the WAV file as the raw request body (Content-Type audio/wav; not multipart) and the model and options in the query string. Send a cached IAM bearer token: IBM says passing the API key directly 'might affect performance', and a token lasts up to 60 minutes. Do not copy the streaming client's audio/l16 content type: IBM warns that its endianness detection can drop the connection on short audio. A request needs at least 100 bytes. One response can hold several results, one for each pause longer than 0.8 seconds, and the adapter must join their transcripts. Asking for audio_metrics=true returns speech_ratio, the closest thing IBM has to a no-speech signal; the map's signal list has no name for it. The 100 concurrent requests of the Plus plan are counted across WebSocket and HTTP together, so a session that falls back to upload must close its socket first and the engine needs a limiter for the whole IBM service instance. The audit's 10 second request timeout is a placeholder with no vendor basis and is not recorded. IBM's asynchronous job API (POST /v1/recognitions, then poll) is not a live transport and is not listed. The gateway's default 16 kHz upload meets this family's 16 kHz minimum.

billing.notes: Only uploaded segments are billed, their padding included. IBM sums usage over the month and rounds at month end, so there is no per-request minimum.

Priced per minute of audio sent. IBM does not round up each call: usage is summed over the month and rounded to the nearest minute at month end, so there is no per-request minimum. Silence is billed like speech, so an open socket bills the whole call. The per-minute price was confirmed only in a pricing page dated 2024-04-19.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1245-1267); the evidence records no live call to IBM. Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). For an id the map does not know, the client passes the string to IBM unchanged (config.rs:597-599). IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST {instance URL}/v1/recognize with the WAV file as the raw request body (Content-Type audio/wav; not multipart) and the model and options in the query string. Send a cached IAM bearer token: IBM says passing the API key directly 'might affect performance', and a token lasts up to 60 minutes. Do not copy the streaming client's audio/l16 content type: IBM warns that its endianness detection can drop the connection on short audio. A request needs at least 100 bytes. One response can hold several results, one for each pause longer than 0.8 seconds, and the adapter must join their transcripts. Asking for audio_metrics=true returns speech_ratio, the closest thing IBM has to a no-speech signal; the map's signal list has no name for it. The 100 concurrent requests of the Plus plan are counted across WebSocket and HTTP together, so a session that falls back to upload must close its socket first and the engine needs a limiter for the whole IBM service instance. The audit's 10 second request timeout is a placeholder with no vendor basis and is not recorded. IBM's asynchronous job API (POST /v1/recognitions, then poll) is not a live transport and is not listed.

billing.notes: Only uploaded segments are billed, their padding included. IBM sums usage over the month and rounds at month end, so there is no per-request minimum.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. IBM's socket accepts many recognition requests on one connection: binary audio, then {"action":"stop"}, then the final results, then {"state":"listening"}, after which the next request needs no new start message. The gateway would keep streaming audio as it arrives and send stop when its own detector reports end of speech, so IBM finalises at once instead of waiting out its 0.8 second pause. Interim results keep arriving while the caller speaks, there is no upload, and the session uses one of the instance's concurrency slots. The latency gain is inferred from the documentation and has not been measured. It is a change to the existing client, not to the shared file-upload adapter.

billing.notes: Priced per minute of audio sent. IBM does not round up each call: usage is summed over the month and rounded to the nearest minute at month end, so there is no per-request minimum. Silence is billed like speech, so an open socket bills the whole call. The per-minute price was confirmed only in a pricing page dated 2024-04-19. No pricing_key: gateway/src/config/pricing.rs has speech-to-text entries only for en-US_Multimedia and en-US_Telephony.

provenance.notes: Default for an IBM model id the map has never seen, for example a new locale or a customer's custom model. The existing streaming client is listed first, as the conversion rule for a working native client requires, so such a session gets what it gets today, with interim results. IBM states that every interface offers the same transcription for every model, so an unknown but valid id streams. The client is not sound: it very probably stops transcribing after 30 seconds of caller silence, and it sends two start-message keys that IBM documents as unavailable for large speech models. The first is recorded in this row's gateway_client.defect; the second matters only for a large speech model id and is recorded on those rows. IBM's synchronous file endpoint, which serves every model family, is listed behind it as a fallback, but no release builds an IBM file transcriber, so that transport is never enabled. The resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. Four ids that the gateway itself produces as language defaults are not IBM models and land on this row: es-LA_Multimedia, zh-CN_Multimedia, ar-MS_Multimedia and hi-IN_Multimedia (gateway/src/core/stt/ibm_watson/config.rs:605, 613, 615, 616). They have no row because the map has no way to mark an id as known to be invalid; the code must remap them to the matching _Telephony or large speech id.
